relevance_note: Single-patient case report of genetically confirmed adult-onset Alexander disease: 'Confirmatory genetic testing identified a pathogenic mutation in the glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) gene'.
method_note: Hand-built with a short Python script in scratch; all values read by me. Two in-scope people: the patient (GFAP pathogenic mutation, variant description not printed, so variant row kept with 'not reported') and her daughter (diagnosed with Alexander's disease; no GFAP testing or variant stated, so no variant row; no individual-level features). Father (cerebrovascular accidents) and mother (beta-thalassemia trait, hypertension, diabetes, hypothyroidism) are neither tested for GFAP nor affected by Alexander disease, so they get no rows. Possible inconsistency: 'the lack of a family history of neurodegenerative disease' (2017 context) vs 'her daughter was also diagnosed with Alexander's disease'. 'Stable and displayed minimal symptoms' vs listed deficits not treated as contradiction. Spasticity/pyramidal signs checklist marked observed from hyperreflexia and positive Hoffman sign (2022 exam); autonomic dysfunction marked observed from nocturnal urinary incontinence (bladder dysfunction). Table 2 labs (WBC 10.54 above range, hemoglobin 9.5 below range) not recorded as features because the paper does not interpret them; normal heart and lung auscultation not recorded. Reference [3] after the diagnosis sentence is a general review, not a prior report of this patient, so cites_prior_report left null. No MRI findings reported, so imaging checklist items are not reported. Age at diagnosis not stated (diagnosis year 2022 only). Table 1 is a generic subtype summary, not patient data. Vital status 'alive' from discharge after surgery.

treatment_summary.value: ergocalciferol 1.25 mg weekly and ferrous sulfate as needed; IUD removal and laparoscopic bilateral tubal sterilization under general anesthesia (midazolam, propofol, rocuronium, sevoflurane, fentanyl; sugammadex and flumazenil reversal)
span: Her medication regimen included 1.25 mg weekly of ergocalciferol and ferrous sulfate, as needed.

successfully underwent intrauterine device (IUD) removal and laparoscopic bilateral tubal sterilization (BTS) under general anesthesia, utilizing midazolam, propofol, rocuronium, and fentanyl without complications
Anesthesia was maintained with inhaled sevoflurane at 2%
sugammadex (200 mg, IV) was administered for the reversal of neuromuscular blockade. In addition, flumazenil (0.2 mg, IV) was given to reverse the effects of midazolam.
